thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Realtime detector: p99 latency breached SLO on /v1/generate (p99=3.4s, threshold=2.5s) — rolling 5m spike, region=us-east-1. Paging oncall.
lee (oncall): On it. Jumping into dashboards now. Any obvious customer-facing errors?
ana (sre): No 5xxs spike in API gateway. Mostly high downstream token generation time. Streaming stall alerts also firing for some sessions.
raj (eng): Could be KV cache pressure or slow kernels. Any recent deploys to inference fleet in us-east-1 in last hour?
emily (product): No customer tickets yet, but usage uptick from a partner integration around 10:12 UTC.
mike (support): I set a watch; will flag customers if we escalate.
lee (oncall): Quick checks: 1) check kvcache hit rate 2) model variant fallback status 3) node CPU/GPU stalls. I'll run metrics queries.
ana (sre): kvcache hit rate dropped from 88% -> 61% in the last 6m for the heavy-chat route. Also see increased retry latency on dedupe service.
raj (eng): That aligns with prefix cache eviction. Can we force-rehydrate cache for the popular prefix? Or enable LRU warming.
lee (oncall): Commands: ``kubectl -n inference scale deployment gen-pool-us-east --replicas=30`` going to try a capacity bump as an immediate mitigation.
incident-bot: Deploy watcher: scale request accepted for gen-pool-us-east, rollout starting.
ana (sre): Rolling CPU/GPU metrics: a subset of GPUs show 95% utilization and occasional memory stalls. Suggest temporarily shifting some traffic to eu-west-1 if capacity available.
raj (eng): We can flip routing policy to prefer eu-west-1 for non-enterprise tenants. Patch in router: ``PATCH /routing/policies/serve?prefer=eu-west-1&selector=!enterprise`` — I'll open the change and keep TTL short.
lee (oncall): Doing safe route-shift: enabling traffic steering to eu-west for 20% initially.
incident-bot: Routing change applied: 20% traffic shifted to eu-west-1 for the affected model. Monitor for 5m.
emily (product): Heads up — partner integration is enterprise tier. We need to exclude enterprise traffic from the shift.
raj (eng): Confirmed, selector used excludes enterprise. Enterprise still in us-east.
mike (support): Notifying the partner success team to standby — message queued.
ana (sre): After scaling + 20% shift, p99 reduced to 2.7s (was 3.4s). Still above SLO but trending down. kvcache hit rate slowly recovering to 72%.
lee (oncall): Good. Next steps: keep scaling to stable levels, investigate root cause of kvcache eviction. I'll trigger a kvcache eviction trace: ``/debug/kvcache/trace?key=prefix-hot``.
raj (eng): I'll look at recent kernel selection logs and model quantization fallback probes. If kvcache was overwhelmed by a traffic pattern (cold-start of many unique prefixes), we may need a short-lived cache-size increase.
ana (sre): Opening incident ticket (INC-2026) with initial mitigation summary and customer-impact: degraded p99 for ~12m, no 5xx, streaming stalls for ~0.5% sessions. Prioritize kvwarm and routing policy audit.
lee (oncall): Paging rotation: ana taking lead on infra triage, raj for runtime, I'll keep oncall thread and coordinate customer comms.
emily (product): If partner experiences degraded UX, we'll put an advisory on status.redwood.ai. Mike, keep me updated on any inbound support tickets.
mike (support): Will do. If we cross 3.0s again, I'll escalate to partner ops.
raj (eng): Quick hypothesis: a small change in client prompt patterns caused cache keys to blow up (conversation IDs + long prefixes). I'll pull sampling from request logs for the last 20m.
ana (sre): We're seeing a spike of very long requests with sequence lengths > 1k which also pushes kernel selection into slower paths. Logging sample attached to ticket.
lee (oncall): For now: 1) keep scaled replicas 2) maintain 20% eu-west steering 3) run kvwarm for top prefixes 4) collect request samples and kernel logs. Check back in 10m.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation checklist updated in INC-2026. Next automated evaluation at +10m.
lee (oncall): Thanks team. I'll update channel with p95/p99 numbers once we have the next 5m window. :thumbsup:
